question: What permanent filesystem policy and exec boundary should OpenClaw support: file-tool path ACLs only, or an OS-backed boundary that also constrains arbitrary shell-mediated access?
rationale: The config shape, default posture, canonicalization semantics, and whether exec is inside the claimed security boundary are security and product choices that competing implementation PRs cannot safely settle independently.

options.title: OS-backed complete boundary
options.body: Specify path policy plus an OS-level sandbox backend so file tools and arbitrary exec share one enforceable filesystem boundary.

options.title: File-tool ACL v1
options.body: Ship normalized deny-wins ACLs for file and media tools while explicitly documenting that unrestricted exec bypasses them.

options.title: Keep workspace-only model
options.body: Decline granular in-process ACLs and direct users to Docker, VM, or per-user isolation for a complete boundary.

recommendation.title: OS-backed complete boundary
recommendation.body: Specify path policy plus an OS-level sandbox backend so file tools and arbitrary exec share one enforceable filesystem boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already framed the unresolved boundary in the discussion and is connected to the current tool-policy implementation history.
